Super Micro Computer (SMCI) has begun shipping new AMD EPYC based all flash storage servers that support the PCIe Gen 6 standard. These products target AI scale data, analytics and high throughput storage workloads.

For investors watching Super Micro Computer, the recent launch of PCIe Gen 6 storage arrives during a tough stretch in the share price. The stock is down about 34% on the 90 day share price return and roughly 25% on the 30 day share price return as legal questions and sector headlines have weighed on sentiment.

Scan how AI infrastructure sentiment is being priced into other hardware plays by reviewing the hand picked 53 AI infrastructure stocks that echo the same Super Micro Computer theme.

Bulls see Super Micro Computer as an AI infrastructure pure play on sale after legal headlines and a sharp share pullback. Bears point to thin AI server margins, customer concentration, and the Justice Department probe. Which case does the current valuation support?

Most Popular Narrative: 56.8% Undervalued

Against a last close of $24.14, the most followed valuation narrative on Super Micro Computer points to a fair value of $55.85 and frames the stock as heavily discounted relative to that anchor, with the gap explained by how investors are treating AI spending cycles and trust risk today. According to RogueEP, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the narrative, the current setup is less about blue sky growth stories and more about what the cash flows look like under tougher assumptions.

SMCI is a good-stock-not-great-company setup: a narrow, cycle-renewed moat and structurally thin margins, but priced at approximately 3.9x our model's FY28E EBITDA with net cash, above-Street revenue momentum and a decaying trust discount. Our framework is appropriately hard-nosed, with an 11.4% WACC which includes a 25 bps FED rate hike, a DCF that embeds a 48% peak-to-trough AI capex bust, and applied multiples at 35-69% discounts to the 10.12x EV/EBITDA and 1.61x EV/REVENUE peer medians. It still produces a $55.85 blended target, 46.6% above our $38.09 reference price.

See why 10 investors see Super Micro Computer as 57% undervalued.

For readers tracking Super Micro Computer, this narrative leans on an 11.4% discount rate and a severe AI spending pullback baked into its cash flow model, yet still lands on a fair value more than double the present share price. The argument is that if those strict inputs hold, the upside case rests less on optimism and more on how quickly sentiment and valuation multiples could shift if legal and margin concerns ease.

title: What Has The Market Missed In Hewlett Packard Enterprise Stock's Drop?

What Has The Market Missed In Hewlett Packard Enterprise Stock's Drop?

Today's big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?

Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) booked record networking orders in fiscal Q3 2026, after buying Juniper Networks. That may be what HPE bulls are betting on. Yet the shares fell 17.5% in the month to November 17, 2026. The S&P 500 fell 4.5% over the same dates. Record orders and a falling share price do not seem to fit together. So how much of that networking demand is HPE turning into sales?

HPE Books Networking Orders Faster Than It Ships

Only part of it, so far. On the September 2, 2026 call, management said orders for its networking gear for AI reached $700 million in fiscal Q3 2026. That was up by triple digits. Cumulative orders for this gear reached $2.2 billion, past the company's target for fiscal 2026. So management raised its year-end target to $2.5 billion to $3 billion.

Sales have moved more slowly. Management said networking orders were growing 3.5 times faster than networking revenue. Networking revenue was $2.9 billion in fiscal Q3 2026, up 10% on management's normalized basis. Management said supply constraints limited how much demand it could turn into revenue. Data center networking revenue fell 6%, which management put down to shipment timing driven by those constraints.

Management expects networking revenue to grow 11% to 13% from a year earlier in fiscal Q4 2026, on order strength and better supply. HPE is shipping more networking gear, just not as fast as customers are ordering it.

Can Networking Hold Up HPE's Margins?

So far, it has. Management said gross margin topped 40% in fiscal Q3 2026 on its own adjusted measure. Disciplined pricing in traditional servers and a larger share of networking helped. Networking earned an operating margin of 22%, against 17% for Cloud & AI, the server and AI systems segment. Both figures are on management's adjusted basis.

HPE expects that difference to last. For fiscal 2027, management's framework puts networking's operating margin in the mid- to high 20% range, against about 13% for Cloud & AI. HPE's networking gear is also part of two recent deals. HPE said on its fiscal Q3 call that Oracle will deploy HPE Juniper routers and switches across one of the largest AI cloud build-outs. On September 30, 2026, HPE announced a $1.2 billion order from Vultr for AMD Helios racks with HPE Networking scale-up switching.

The worry for a holder is one management raised itself. It expects gross margin to move back toward more historical levels as AI systems grow and traditional server pricing normalizes, with more networking offsetting that. It also expects the company's operating margin to fall in fiscal Q4 2026 from fiscal Q3. The main causes are a higher mix of AI systems and pricing.

title: Wife of senior Nvidia executive embroiled in chip smuggling scandal
detail:
Wife of senior Nvidia executive embroiled in chip smuggling scandal
Matthew Field
Wed, November 18, 2026 at 7:38 AM MST 3 min read
NVDA
SMCI
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Jay Puri, an Nvidia executive, and Cenly Chen, who worked at Super Micro

The wife of one of Jensen Huang's most senior allies has been caught up in a chip-smuggling scandal that has engulfed one of Nvidia's biggest partners.

Cenly Chen, who is reportedly married to Jay Puri, an Nvidia executive, worked at Super Micro, a technology company where senior executives have been accused of smuggling $2.5bn (£1.9bn) worth of chips to China.

In a lawsuit brought by shareholders of Super Micro, investors allege there was "no way Cenly Chen lacked knowledge about the company's illicit sales". Super Micro has yet to file a response to the claims.

Ms Chen was previously chief growth officer at Super Micro, which packages Nvidia chips into computer servers.

US prosecutors charged some of the company's leading executives earlier this year over involvement in an illicit chip smuggling scheme.

Super Micro has insisted it has co-operated with the US government's investigation and has not been named in its indictment. Ms Chen is not named in the US charges.

However, the revelations come amid mounting scrutiny on Nvidia's ties to the Far East over claims Mr Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Muddy waters, a short-selling firm, raised questions over Ms Chen's ties to Nvidia on Tuesday night.

The firm noted how Ms Chen had been repeatedly photographed alongside Mr Puri and named in photographs as Cenly Puri.

The pair are reportedly married, technology news site The Information reported on Wednesday.

Nvidia has already been the subject of intense pressure over claims that Chinese companies sought to access its chips through illegal smuggling and legal loopholes.

Nvidia's graphics chips are widely used to develop powerful AI technology.

The Super Micro scandal, which emerged earlier this year, saw Wally Liaw, the company's co-founder, charged by the US government for allegedly diverting advanced Nvidia chips via Taiwan to customers in China.

Mr Liaw has pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Mr Huang resigned last Thursday over claims he had a relationship with Alice Huang, who worked at another Nvidia customer, Megaspeed.

Megaspeed, based in Singapore, has also been investigated by the US for smuggling over claims it diverted powerful Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.

Nvidia's board rejected an attempt by Mr Huang to return to the company on Tuesday, insisting it had no plans to reinstate him.

The fallout has also triggered scrutiny in the White House.

It emerged on Wednesday that leading Democrats in the US House of Representatives have launched an investigation into whether Howard Lutnick, the US commerce secretary, had used his position to help Cantor Fitzgerald avoid losses from the Nvidia scandal.

Why Is Super Micro Computer Stock Rising Today?

Blue chart going up ©Adobe Stock Images

Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) shares climbed 4.3% in US premarket trading, supported by a broader recovery in artificial intelligence infrastructure stocks following stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings from Nvidia.

The advance followed Nvidia's November 17 earnings announcement, which included an improved revenue growth outlook for 2028 and helped restore confidence in continued investment in AI computing infrastructure.

Supermicro's gains came after a difficult period for the stock, which had been affected by regulatory concerns, reports of a major customer cancellation and selling by senior company insiders.

The recovery also extended to other AI server manufacturers, suggesting that improving industry sentiment was the primary driver of the latest advance rather than a resolution of Supermicro's company-specific challenges.

How Did Nvidia's Earnings Boost Supermicro Shares?

Nvidia's latest quarterly results provided a significant catalyst for the recovery in artificial intelligence and semiconductor-related stocks.

The chipmaker reported stronger-than-expected earnings on November 17 and raised its revenue growth target for 2028, reinforcing expectations that demand for AI computing infrastructure remains substantial.

The announcement helped reverse a five-session losing streak in technology shares, with S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures advancing sharply ahead of Wednesday's market opening.

For Supermicro, the results were particularly relevant because the company manufactures high-performance servers and computing systems used in artificial intelligence data centres.

Continued demand for Nvidia's advanced processors can support demand for the server infrastructure required to deploy those chips.

The stronger outlook therefore provided a positive signal for companies involved in supplying AI computing equipment.

Supermicro's 4.3% premarket gain reflected renewed investor confidence in the broader AI infrastructure market following several sessions of selling pressure.

Why Has Supermicro Stock Been Under Pressure?

Supermicro shares have experienced substantial weakness amid a combination of company-specific concerns and broader technology sector volatility.

One of the most significant issues has been a reported US Department of Justice investigation into whether entities linked to the company's co-founder helped divert Supermicro products to China in violation of US export controls.

The reported investigation has created uncertainty surrounding the company's regulatory exposure and potential legal risks.

title: Can Super Micro Computer Stock Jump 50%?

Can Super Micro Computer Stock Jump 50%?

Today's big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?

For Super Micro Computer (SMCI) stock to jump 50%, the company most likely has to deliver a much bigger year. Management forecast that year on November 3, 2026. Moves that size are common for this stock. In 9 of the 10 calendar years from 2016 to 2025, it rose at least 50% from one close to a later close in the same year. The stock has gone the other way so far: the shares fell 33.7% over the past twelve months, while the S&P 500 returned 10.3%. For the bigger year to happen, Super Micro has to ship the orders it already holds as customer sites get ready. Management also built its range on underlying sales that keep rising after a one-time catch-up drops out. So what has management told investors to expect, and is any of it showing up yet?

Super Micro Expects Much Bigger Sales In Fiscal 2027

Management now expects fiscal 2027 revenue of $72 billion to $82 billion, up from the $65 billion to $72 billion it expected a quarter earlier. Super Micro ended the first quarter with what management called a record backlog. AI solutions made up about 71% of first-quarter revenue, against 59% in the quarter before.

Shipping is running ahead of plan so far. First-quarter revenue reached $19.9 billion, coming in above the $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion management had guided. About $2.3 billion of that total came from deployments first scheduled for earlier periods, leaving underlying revenue near $17.6 billion. Management said the pace from here comes down to how fast customer facilities become ready and how freely key components arrive, not to demand.

How Big Is Fiscal 2027 Against Super Micro Today?

Even the low end of the new range sits well above the $39.1 billion Super Micro reported for fiscal 2026. It also clears the $54.0 billion the company reported over the twelve months to September 30, 2026.

On simple arithmetic, the low end of the range does not need growth after the catch-up. To reach $72 billion, the last three quarters of the year need at least $52.1 billion between them. That is about $17.4 billion a quarter, a little below the first quarter's underlying $17.6 billion. Management guided the second quarter to $19.5 billion to $21.5 billion. Management still built its full-year range on continued growth in underlying demand, without a repeat of the catch-up.

The share price appears to assume far less. Super Micro stock closed 51.9% below its highest close of the past year, set on June 2, 2026. Even a 50% jump from that close would leave the shares below that high. It trades at 4.3 times its trailing twelve-month earnings, against 22.0 for the S&P 500.
